records.name: Bauchi
records.summary:
For a trans traveler Bauchi means exposure to a religious criminal code with a capital ceiling: the religious penal code of this state/province remains in force (a June 2025 government note confirms it), and its courts are on record as the place where the ultimate penalty was actually pronounced - in June 2022 a religious court in the town of Ningi sentenced three men, including a 70-year-old, to death by stoning for same-sex acts after a religious-police arrest, the first time the death penalty had actually been imposed for homosexuality in the country. The sentence was pronounced, not carried out: no execution is on record, the accused were released on bail pending appeal, and the June 2025 note records the sentence could not be carried out until ratified by the governor of this state/province.

Practical safety: the moral code is actively enforced - the same government note places a further death-by-stoning sentence for homosexuality from a religious court in this state/province in May 2024, and advisory material in 2025-26 continues to cite corporal enforcement of religio

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (Reuters returns 401 to automated fetches); the underlying Reuters report (2 July 2022) covers the Ningi Sharia court sentencing three men - a 70-year-old among them - to death by stoning for homosexuality after a 14 June 2022 Hisbah arrest, the first time the death penalty has actually been imposed for homosexuality in Nigeria.

Amnesty International press release (2004): the Upper Sharia Court of Bauchi State quashed Jubrin Babaji's death-by-stoning 'sodomy' sentence (convicted 25 September 2003 under Section 133 of the Bauchi Sharia Penal Code Law 2001) for denial of counsel and a defective confession, following the quashing of Yunusa Rafin Chiyawa's conviction on 14 November 2003 - 'a number of cases where convictions and sentences to death have been quashed on appeal'. Also records a then-pending stoning appeal (Usman/Ibrahim) before a Sharia Court of Appeal in Niger State.

UK Home Office country policy and information note, June 2025, confirming the Sharia Penal Codes of the twelve northern states, including Bauchi, remain in force. The note records that a Sharia court in Bauchi sentenced three men to death by stoning for 'homosexual acts' in 2022 but that the sentence could not be carried out until ratified by the state governor, and that a further report placed a death-by-stoning sentence for homosexuality from a Sharia court in Bauchi in May 2024. It also records that at a sodomy trial in January 2014 at Bauchi's Tudun Alkali Upper Sharia Court an angry mob stormed the premises demanding a death sentence. This is the June 2025 government note the record cites for the code remaining in force and for the 2022 sentence having been pronounced but not executed.

THISDAY, 3 July 2022: a Sharia court sitting in Ningi local government area of Bauchi State sentenced three men to death by stoning for homosexuality, among them 70-year-old Malam Haruna, based on Section 134 of the Bauchi State Penal Law of 2001. The prosecution was brought by members of the Hisbah Vanguard through Adamu Dan Kafi, who told the court the three were arrested committing the offence at Gwada village, Ningi LGA on 14 June 2022. Second national Nigerian paper confirming that Bauchi's Sharia court actually pronounced the stoning sentence this record is about.

Punch report of the 28 June 2022 Ningi Sharia Court death-by-stoning sentence against three men in Bauchi State, built on interviews with relatives, published 16 July 2022. It records that presiding Shariah judge Munka'ilu Sabo-Ningi held the men violated Section 134 of the Bauchi State Penal Law of 2001, that a 30-day appeal window was granted, and - through relatives of the convicted men - that the judgment had not been carried out at the time of reporting. Confirms both the pronouncement of the sentence and the absence of any execution on record that the summary relies on.

records.name: Sokoto
records.summary:
For a trans traveler Sokoto is a statutory-exposure record with verified court-level enforcement: the religious penal code of this state/province took effect on 31 January 2001; male same-sex activity draws death by stoning for married or previously-married offenders and 100 lashes for the unmarried, while acts between women draw a discretionary sentence of up to 100 lashes and/or imprisonment. A June 2025 government note confirms the code remains in force.

Practical safety: a 2019 rights-monitoring study of 173 religious-court cases (2017) covers this state/province among its three sample states/provinces, confirming operational religious courts and religious-police activity here; no capital sentence is on record as imposed in this state/province - that record belongs to a neighbouring state/province - and no trans-specific incident is documented.

sources.summary: Equaldex log entry #14118: the Sharia Penal Code Laws took effect in Sokoto on 31 January 2001; male same-sex activity is punished by stoning to death where the offender is or has been married, and 100 lashes otherwise; sexual acts between women (wsafa) draw ta'azir punishment of up to 100 lashes and/or imprisonment.

This chapter of the academic sourcebook reproduces the full record of a capital prosecution in Sokoto State's Sharia courts. On 9 October 2001 the Upper Sharia Court at Gwadabawa (Sokoto State) convicted Safiyatu Hussaini Tungar Tudu of zina under sections 128-129 of the Sokoto State Sharia Penal Code and sentenced her to death by stoning, while the co-accused was discharged and acquitted. On her appeal, filed 26 October 2001, the Sharia Court of Appeal of Sokoto State quashed the conviction and discharged and acquitted her on 25 March 2002. For this record the document evidences that Sokoto's religious courts apply the state Sharia Penal Code in practice, including the same capital-punishment framework (for zina, not same-sex conduct) the code carries for married men's same-sex acts.

Primary committee reports mapping Sokoto's Sharia adoption: the interim report was submitted to Sokoto Governor Attahiru Dalhatu Bafarawa on 13 October 1999 and the final report on 16 December 1999, with an annexe draft bill to establish Sharia courts applying Sharia law in Sokoto State. They document the state-level groundwork for the Sokoto Sharia Penal Code - in force from 31 January 2001 per this record's other sources - that carries the stoning and lashing penalties for men's same-sex acts described in this record.
